To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the effects of news consumption on political knowledge, political interest, and political participation are stronger when the news is consumed on a computer than a mobile device; (2) news consumption on a computer has a positive effect on political participation, while the same is not true of mobile device news consumption; (3) news consumption on computers has a positive effect in the relationship between political knowledge and political participation, while news consumption on mobile devices has a negative effect on this relationship;

1) news engagement on computers and laptops is more robust than on mobile devices; 2) news engagement is more robust on high speed connections than on slower connections; and 3) the effects of connection speed on news engagement are more pronounced among Latino audiences than among the total U.S population.

1) news engagement and political knowledge are higher on a laptop than on a tablet, and 2) news engagement and knowledge are higher on laptop than on a smartphone, and 3) the difference between tablet and smartphone news engagement and knowledge is small.

the impact of the changing media environment, particularly as it relates to mobile connectivity, on political learning and news engagement.
the consequences of the proliferation of the Internet, and mobile devices for political knowledge and engagement.
the consequences of access and connectivity on the political information seeking behaviors of ordinary Americans.
